# Disagreement Log — 1 Maccabees Chapter 7

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Translators:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 34

---

## Disagreement Entries

**1MA 7:1 — "came out from Rome" vs. "escaped from Rome"**
- EMET: "came out from Rome"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "escaped from Rome"
- RULING: "escaped from Rome" — Demetrius had been a hostage in Rome and fled without authorization; "escaped" is historically accurate and supported by Polybius 31.11

**1MA 7:1 — "went up with a few men to a city by the sea"**
- EMET: "went up with a few men to a city by the sea"
- LOGOS: "came with a few men to a coastal city"
- PNEUMA: "landed at a city on the coast"
- RULING: "arrived with a few men at a coastal city" — LOGOS formulation is clearest

**1MA 7:3 — "Do not show me their face" vs. "Do not let me see their faces"**
- EMET: "Do not show me their face"
- LOGOS: "Do not let me see their faces"
- PNEUMA: "Don't bring them in front of me"
- RULING: "Do not let me see their faces" — LOGOS; the refusal is a command not to display the captives; plural "faces" is appropriate

**1MA 7:5 — "came to him" — the delegation of renegades**
- All translators agree on the subject. No disagreement.

**1MA 7:5 — "led them" vs. "led the pack" vs. "was leading them"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "Alcimus...led them"
- PNEUMA: "Leading the pack was Alcimus"
- RULING: "led by Alcimus" — passive construction cleaner; PNEUMA's "leading the pack" is too colloquial

**1MA 7:6 — "all your friends" vs. "all your loyal men"**
- EMET/LOGOS/PNEUMA: all render *tous philous sou* as "your friends"
- RULING: "all your friends" — the court title *philoi* is preserved by all; no disagreement

**1MA 7:8 — "Great Plain" — all agree to preserve the geographic name**
- The *megalē pedion* = Great Plain (the Jezreel Valley region). All preserve it. No disagreement.

**1MA 7:8 — "great and faithful to the king" vs. "a powerful man, faithful to the king"**
- EMET: "great and faithful to the king"
- LOGOS: "a great man, faithful to the king"
- PNEUMA: "a powerful man and loyal"
- RULING: "a powerful man, faithful to the king" — LOGOS; "great" is ambiguous; "powerful" is more precise for *megas*

**1MA 7:10 — "words of peace deceitfully" vs. "deceptively peaceful words"**
- EMET: "with words of peace deceitfully"
- LOGOS: "deceptively peaceable words"
- PNEUMA: "smooth, peaceful language — lies"
- RULING: "peaceable words — spoken in deceit" — separating peace-language from deceptive intent is important

**1MA 7:12 — "company of scribes" — the *grammateis***
- EMET/LOGOS: "company of scribes"
- PNEUMA: "delegation of scholars"
- RULING: "company of scribes" — *sunagoge grammateon* = an assembly of Torah-scholars; LOGOS/EMET are closer; PNEUMA's "scholars" is acceptable but less precise

**1MA 7:13 — "seed of Aaron" vs. "line of Aaron" vs. "lineage of Aaron"**
- EMET: "seed of Aaron"
- LOGOS: "line of Aaron"
- PNEUMA: (paraphrases)
- RULING: "lineage of Aaron" — *spermatos Aaron* = seed/lineage of Aaron; "lineage" is clearer than "seed" in English

**1MA 7:14 — "spoke to them words of peace and swore to them"**
- EMET/LOGOS: same substance
- RULING: "Alcimus spoke peaceful words to them and swore an oath" (LOGOS)

**1MA 7:15 — "according to the word which was written"**
- EMET: "according to the word which was written"
- LOGOS: "in accordance with the scripture that says"
- PNEUMA: "fulfilling the scripture that says"
- RULING: "in accordance with the word that was written" — EMET/LOGOS; the Greek *kata ton logon hon egrapse* is literally "according to the word that was written"; PNEUMA's "fulfilling" is an interpretation

**1MA 7:16 — "flesh of your holy ones" vs. "flesh of your faithful ones"**
- EMET: "holy ones"
- LOGOS: "faithful ones"
- PNEUMA: (follows LOGOS)
- RULING: "faithful ones" — *hosion sou* = your devout/faithful ones; in the LXX of Ps. 79:2 *hasidecha* = your faithful/devoted ones; "faithful" is more accurate

**1MA 7:17 — "There is no truth and no judgment in them"**
- EMET: "no truth and no judgment"
- LOGOS: "no truth or justice"
- RULING: "no truth or justice" — LOGOS; "judgment" for *krisis* here means justice/just dealings

**1MA 7:18 — "great cistern" — all agree**
- All translators preserve "great cistern." No disagreement. This is a specific geographic feature.

**1MA 7:20 — "struggling for his high priesthood" vs. "fought to maintain his hold" vs. "fought to hold his grip"**
- EMET: "struggling for his high priesthood"
- LOGOS: "fought to maintain his hold on the high priesthood"
- PNEUMA: "fought to hold his grip on the high priesthood"
- RULING: "fought to hold his grip on the high priesthood" — the competition for the priesthood is one of the key political subplots; PNEUMA's "grip" conveys the precariousness

**1MA 7:22 — "evil worse than the nations" vs. "harm worse than the Gentiles had done"**
- EMET: "evil worse than the nations"
- LOGOS: "harm worse than the Gentiles had done"
- RULING: "harm worse than the Gentiles had done" — LOGOS; "the nations" = Gentiles; "harm" is more precise than "evil"

**1MA 7:23 — "restrained from going into the land"**
- EMET: "restrained from going into the land"
- LOGOS: "prevented from going about in the country"
- PNEUMA: "cut off their freedom of movement"
- RULING: "cut off from going through the land" — LOGOS/PNEUMA; the restriction of movement is the key point

**1MA 7:25 — "honored princes" vs. "honored princes" — "enemy and hated Israel"**
- EMET: "one of his honored princes, who was an enemy and hated Israel"
- LOGOS: "one of his honored princes, a bitter enemy of Israel"
- PNEUMA: "one of his most distinguished commanders, a man who loathed Israel"
- RULING: "one of his honored princes — a man hostile to Israel and bitter against them" — preserving both elements of the characterization

**1MA 7:26 — "words of peace deceitfully" — second occurrence of this formula**
- EMET: "with words of peace deceitfully"
- LOGOS: "deceptively peaceable words"
- RULING: "deceitfully peaceable words" — same as v.10 ruling

**1MA 7:27 — "see each other's faces in peace" vs. "meet face to face in peace"**
- EMET: "see each other's faces in peace"
- LOGOS: "meet one another in peace"
- PNEUMA: "talk face to face"
- RULING: "meet face to face in peace" — compromise; the idiom of "face to face" carries the peaceable pretense

**1MA 7:28 — "greeted each other peaceably" — the staged meeting**
- All translators agree on the staging of the false peace meeting. No disagreement.

**1MA 7:34 — "laughed at them and mocked them, and defiled them"**
- EMET: "laughed at them and mocked them, and defiled them"
- LOGOS: "mocked them, derided them, defiled them"
- PNEUMA: "laughed at them. He mocked them. He treated them with contempt."
- RULING: "he mocked them, derided them, and defiled them" — LOGOS; the triple defilement is in the text; "laughed" (*kategelasas*) and "mocked" (*katemukterisas*) are distinct; LOGOS preserves both

**1MA 7:35 — "swore with wrath" vs. "In anger he swore an oath" vs. "made an oath in fury"**
- EMET: "swore with wrath"
- LOGOS: "In anger he swore an oath"
- PNEUMA: "made an oath in fury"
- RULING: "In great wrath he swore an oath" — EMET's "with wrath" + LOGOS construction

**1MA 7:35 — "burn this house" — all agree on the sacrilegious threat**
- All translators preserve the exact threat about burning the temple. No disagreement.

**1MA 7:37 — "house of prayer and supplication"**
- All translators agree. This echoes Solomon's dedication prayer (1 Kings 8:29-30) and Isaiah 56:7. No disagreement.

**1MA 7:41 — "blasphemed" vs. "spoke blasphemies"**
- EMET: "blasphemed"
- LOGOS: "spoke blasphemies"
- RULING: "blasphemed" — simpler and equally accurate

**1MA 7:41 — "a hundred and eighty-five thousand" — all agree**
- The number is preserved by all. Reference to 2 Kings 19:35. No disagreement.

**1MA 7:42 — "spoken evilly against your sanctuary" vs. "spoken wickedly against"**
- EMET: "spoke evilly against"
- LOGOS: "spoken viciously against"
- PNEUMA: "what he said about your sanctuary"
- RULING: "spoken wickedly against your sanctuary" — balanced between EMET and LOGOS

**1MA 7:47 — "right arm which he had stretched out with great pride"**
- EMET: "right arm which he had stretched out with great pride"
- LOGOS: "right arm, which he had stretched out in arrogance"
- PNEUMA: "the arm he had raised in his arrogance"
- RULING: "right arm, which he had stretched out with arrogance" — the right arm = the threatening arm; LOGOS/EMET formulation adopted

**1MA 7:48 — "day of great gladness" vs. "great festival"**
- EMET: "day of great gladness"
- LOGOS: "great festival"
- RULING: "day of great gladness" — *hemera... euphrosunes megales* = a day of great joy; "festival" interprets rather than translates

**1MA 7:49 — Nicanor's Day — all agree on 13 Adar**
- All translators agree. The institution of the festival is rendered identically. No disagreement.

**1MA 7:50 — "for a little while"**
- EMET/LOGOS/PNEUMA all agree on this understated closing. No disagreement.
